clusters.text: A UT poll shows Vikki Goodwin leading Dan Patrick 49% to 46% in the Lieutenant Governor race.
clusters.verdict_basis: The UT/Texas Politics Project's own release of Oct. 14, 2026 lists the Lt. Governor result as Patrick 46%, Goodwin 49%, Libertarian Anthony Cristo 2%, Green Party candidate Kevin McCormick 1%, and "someone else" 2%. The poll surveyed 1,200 registered voters from Sept. 25 to Oct. 5, with a ±2.83-point margin of error. The Texas Tribune, KXAN and WFAA all report the same 49%–46% figure. The claim's numbers and attribution are accurate. One caveat is that the 3-point gap is within the poll's margin of error for likely voters. The UT release itself describes Democratic leads as narrow and within that margin, and the Tribune calls them "razor-thin." The claim doesn't say otherwise, so I don't treat it as misleading.

clusters.text: The author, a 62-year-old woman with a nursing master's degree, will vote Republican for every office on the ballot.
clusters.verdict_basis:
The claim is an unattributed first-person statement about a private person's age, education and future vote. I found no letter, op-ed or post that identifies the author, and no record or poll release that could confirm any of those details. The searches returned only race context: 
Patrick won his March primary outright and Goodwin took the Democratic nomination in May
 (Texas Tribune). The Houston Chronicle and Austin American-Statesman editorial boards have also endorsed Goodwin. None of this speaks to this author's age, degree or ballot choices. A stated intention to vote also can't be checked, because ballots are secret and the vote hasn't happened yet. The claim is neither confirmed nor contradicted.

clusters.text: Kalshi betting markets give Dan Patrick a 74% chance and Vikki Goodwin a 26% chance in the lieutenant governor race.
clusters.verdict_basis:
I found no record of Kalshi's Texas Lt. Governor market on or near Sept. 20, 2026, so the claimed 74%/26% split can't be checked. The nearby snapshots I found all differ from it:
- 
Kalshi's own page, captured about 66 days before the election, showed Patrick at 86% and Goodwin at 21%.

- 
A Kalshi tracker snapshot from Oct. 1 listed Patrick at 71%.

- 
A Kalshi-sourced aggregator, updated Oct. 14, showed Patrick at 73% and Goodwin at 28%.


The claimed figures are plausible and close to these readings, but none matches them. The Oct. 14 prices are 73 and 28, which add up to more than 100, so a clean 74/26 pair looks like a rounded or normalized figure rather than a quoted Kalshi price. Patrick has been the clear market favorite throughout, but this is a thin market, and I could not find a dated Sept. 20 price to confirm or contradict the exact numbers.

clusters.text: Kalshi markets give James Talarico a 60% chance of beating Ken Paxton in the Texas Senate race.
clusters.verdict_basis:
Kalshi's own market write-ups show Talarico's price moving over the weeks around the claim. It was 51% on Sept. 14 (
per OddsShopper
) and 59% by Sept. 22 (
per DeFi Rate
). Kalshi's news site then reported 
60% for Talarico and 40% for Paxton
 in a post dated Sept. 28, eight days after the claim first appeared. Later prices were 63% (Oct. 9), 64% (Oct. 12) and 
65% on Kalshi as of October 14
. I found no record of the exact Kalshi price on Sept. 20, but the nearest data points are 59% on Sept. 22 and 58% in a Kalshi post citing a Sept. 23 Marist poll, so a flat "60%" is roughly right but not exact for that date. It is also not the current price. The Dan Patrick/Vikki Goodwin context is a different race and does not affect the Talarico–Paxton market. Because the exact figure is unconfirmed for the date and the price has since moved, I rate it misleading rather than supported.

clusters.text: Texas Ranger David Maxwell, Ken Paxton's former top law enforcement agent, is endorsing James Talarico.
clusters.verdict_basis:
The Texas Tribune (via KWTX and KSAT) reported on Sept. 8, 2026 that 
David Maxwell, the former top cop under Attorney General Ken Paxton, has endorsed Paxton's opponent, James Talarico, for U.S. Senate.
 The Austin American-Statesman reported that 
he is a former Texas Ranger who became Paxton's top law enforcement official before testifying against him at the impeachment trial, and that he endorsed Talarico in a new campaign ad.
 The Center Square said 
he was Paxton's Director of Law Enforcement and a longtime Texas Ranger.
 The Hill also lists him as a founding member of Talarico's Republican-backers group. The claim's wording ("Texas Ranger," "former top law enforcement agent," "endorsing Talarico") matches this reporting. The only quibble is that "Texas Ranger" is a former title, which the claim's own phrasing "former … agent" largely covers. The claim never mentions the Senate race, so it fits with the Lt. Gov. race context only as a separate, accurate statement about Talarico's Senate campaign.

clusters.text: Vikki Goodwin filed a police report accusing Dan Patrick of violating Texas law over AI-generated videos of her in campaign ads.
clusters.verdict_basis:
The claim is accurate as worded. The Texas Tribune (as quoted by Joe.My.God), KUT, the Houston Chronicle and KERA all report that Goodwin filed a police report. 
She filed it with the Travis County Sheriff's Office on Saturday, per her campaign
. The report 
accuses Patrick of violating Texas law over two ads with AI-generated videos of Goodwin
. 
The sheriff's office confirmed it received the complaint.
 Goodwin cited the 2019 deepfake law, and Patrick's campaign called the videos "obvious parody" and disputed that they fell within the law's 30-day window. The claim only says she accused him of a violation, and it does not say a violation was established. Because it stops there, the dispute over whether the law applies does not make it misleading.

clusters.text: If Democrats win the governor and lieutenant governor races in Texas, Gina Hinojosa could be considered for the 2028 Democratic VP nomination.
Republicans increasingly fear losing the Senate and governor's races in Texas.
clusters.verdict_basis:
Reporting strongly supports the Senate half of the claim. CNN reported in August that 
Texas Republicans are openly worried about losing a statewide race for the first time in three decades
. POLITICO reported that 
Republicans are increasingly worried MAGA Inc. won't throw down in time
 to help Paxton. Polls back this up: Marist (Oct. 8–11) has 
Talarico 47%, Paxton 45% among likely voters
, and the Hill reports the race has tightened since September. The governor's race is different. 
Most polls still show Abbott leading, though the race has tightened
, and Abbott 
told reporters, "I'm not concerned at all"
. The sources I found show Abbott attacking harder and spending on ads, but none directly report Republicans fearing a loss in that race, so "fear" there is inference. The claim treats both races the same, and the evidence is much weaker for governor. A Texas Tribune-reported poll does show Democrat Vikki Goodwin 
leading Patrick 49% to 46%
, but the claim doesn't mention the lieutenant governor's race.

clusters.text: A TPOR poll shows James Talarico leading Ken Paxton 49% to 44%.
clusters.verdict_basis:
Texas Public Opinion Research (TPOR) published its September poll, and it has Talarico at 49% and Paxton at 44% in the U.S. Senate race. 
The TPOR release gives Talarico (49%) a five-point lead over Paxton (44%).
 The Hill and Fox 7 Austin report the same numbers. 
The Hill says the survey was conducted Sept. 19-22 with 1,007 respondents and a 3.6-point margin of error.
 270toWin lists the poll as dated 9/25/2026, which matches the date the claim first appeared on X. The claim leaves out the margin of error, which is a minor omission. The 5-point lead is also only slightly outside that margin if it is read as applying to each candidate's share. The wording of the claim matches the poll's topline.

clusters.text: A Texas Republican outside the RNC event in Dallas is endorsing James Talarico because of Ken Paxton's corruption.
clusters.verdict_basis:
I found no report or record of the specific scene in the claim, which is an unnamed Republican speaking outside the RNC event in Dallas and endorsing Talarico over Paxton's corruption. The wider context is well documented. The RNC midterm convention ran in Dallas from Sept. 9 to 10. 
Talarico announced "Republicans for Talarico" on the second and final day of the GOP midterm convention in Dallas

"I will support plenty of Republicans this November, but I cannot vote for Ken Paxton."

"continues to enrich himself at the expense of working people."
 The Dallas Morning News also reports that Democrats and Talarico 
have tried to paint Paxton as morally corrupt.

clusters.text: Ken Paxton is corrupt.
A poll shows Gina Hinojosa leading Greg Abbott by four points (49% to 45%).
clusters.verdict_basis:
The ReconMR/Siena Research Institute poll, released Sept. 17, 2026, found Hinojosa ahead of Abbott 49% to 45%. 
Fox 7 Austin reports it was fielded Sept. 8–11 among 614 likely voters, with a margin of error of ±4.3%.
 KXAN (Nexstar) 
also reports the 49%–45% result and calls it the first poll to show Hinojosa ahead.
 So the figures and the date match the claim. The claim leaves out that the four-point lead is inside the margin of error. It is also one poll among many. 
Fox News/Beacon-Shaw had Abbott up 52–47 in late September.
 
A separate Texas Public Opinion Research poll, fielded Sept. 19–22, had Abbott 50%, Hinojosa 46%.
 The claim only says "a poll shows", and it describes that poll accurately.

clusters.text: Dan Patrick told supporters he and Greg Abbott have tight races and that Ken Paxton is tied with James Talarico.
clusters.verdict_basis:
Quorum Report (republished by livtx.org) reported that Patrick told supporters at an Austin Club fundraiser on a Wednesday that he and Abbott were in tight races. 
Its account says Patrick told supporters he and Abbott are both in tight races while Paxton is tied with Talarico.
 
Attendees said he told the crowd both he and Abbott would win if the election were held today "as long as everything goes right."
 
Per that account, he said Paxton is "essentially tied" with Talarico.
 The "essentially" softens the claim's "tied" slightly.

The caveats are that this is a single outlet, and it relies on unnamed attendees and sources, with "apparently" in its own wording. I found no recording, transcript or on-record statement from Patrick's campaign. Public polls from mid-October are consistent with a tight picture, though they post-date the fundraiser. 
The UT/Texas Politics Project poll has Talarico up 50–47, Hinojosa up 49–48 over Abbott, and Goodwin up 49–46 over Patrick.


The claim matches the only available report, but that report is secondhand.

clusters.text: Ken Paxton beat his impeachment, which was a sham.
A Stratus Intelligence poll shows Ken Paxton and James Talarico tied at 48% in the Texas Senate race.
clusters.verdict_basis: Breitbart (Sept. 29) reported that a Stratus Intelligence survey of 865 likely voters, conducted Sept. 22–24, had Paxton and Talarico each at 48%, with 4% undecided. Newsweek's polling roundup gives the same figures: a 48–48 tie, with the same sample size and field dates. Both outlets say the poll was commissioned by Texans for a Conservative Majority, a Republican group. The claim doesn't mention that sponsor, but its numbers, pollster and race are accurate. Other polls differ. Marist had Talarico ahead 50–44 in September, and the UT/Texas Politics Project had him ahead 50–47 in October. The claim doesn't say otherwise.

clusters.text: Ken Paxton will be the next US senator from Texas.
Donations to Ken Paxton are tied to a company that facilitates Chinese real estate investments in Texas.
clusters.verdict_basis:
A Houston Chronicle/Hearst Newspapers review of campaign finance records found that 
Paxton's campaign took in $40,000 from donors who work for companies that facilitate Chinese investments in Texas real estate
. 
Most of the donations are linked to Wan Bridge, a U.S.-based real estate development company that solicits foreign investors for its Texas housing developments.
 The donors were Wan Bridge's cofounders, 
Ting Qiao (nearly $30,000) and Danting Li (just over $10,000)
. The Chronicle also tied a third donor, 
John Chiang, to a U.S. development firm that contracts with Wan Bridge
. Two wording points: the money came from individuals who work for or co-founded these firms, not from the company itself, and a second firm is involved. Even so, "tied to a company that facilitates Chinese real estate investments" fits the reporting, which Courier Texas and The Real Deal repeated. The Chronicle noted the donations were 
far from the largest to Paxton's campaign
, and 
Paxton's spokesperson did not address questions about them
. I did not check the FEC filings directly, and the claim's Dan Patrick/Goodwin framing does not match its Paxton subject.

clusters.text: A TPOR poll shows Greg Abbott leading Gina Hinojosa 50% to 46%.
clusters.verdict_basis:
Texas Public Opinion Research (TPOR) published its September poll on its Substack. 
It has Republican Greg Abbott at 50% and Democrat Gina Hinojosa at 46% in the governor's race, a four-point lead.
 RealClearPolling lists the same result: 
a TPOR poll of 1,007 likely voters, fielded 9/19–9/22, showing 50 to 46 (Abbott +4).
 That matches the claim's numbers, the pollster and the candidates. The claim was first seen on 2026-09-25, after the poll's release. One caveat is that TPOR's own numbers show 
Abbott's lead narrowed from +7 in August to +4
. Other pollsters at the time showed a closer race, and some had Hinojosa ahead. The claim only says what the TPOR poll shows, so that context doesn't make it inaccurate.

clusters.text: A ReconMR/Siena poll shows James Talarico leading Ken Paxton 49% to 43%.
clusters.verdict_basis:
The 49%–43% figure is real, but it comes from ReconMR alone, not from a ReconMR/Siena poll. 
ReconMR's Texas Poll found Talarico ahead 49% to 43% among 614 likely voters surveyed by phone and text on Sept. 8–11.
 
Newsmax reported the same numbers: it was released Thursday (Sept. 17) and had a 4.3-point margin of error.
 Siena's polls are separate New York Times/Siena surveys with different results. 
The June poll showed a 47%–47% tie.
 
The Sept. 21–30 poll showed Talarico ahead 51% to 45%.
 I found no joint "ReconMR/Siena" poll. One aggregator, Newscord, did mention a "ReconMR/Siena" poll at 48%–44%, but that appears to be a garbled label and the numbers don't match the claim. Because the numbers are right but the pollster attribution is wrong, the claim is misleading.

clusters.text: A TSU poll shows James Talarico leading Ken Paxton 47% to 46%.
clusters.verdict_basis:
Texas Southern University's Barbara Jordan Public Policy Research and Survey Center released a Senate poll in September 2026. 
It showed Talarico leading Paxton 47% to 46%.
 
The poll was conducted Sept. 15–19 with 1,800 likely voters.
 
Its margin of error was 2.3 percent.
 Fox 7 Austin, The Texan, and The Center Square report the same figures. 270toWin lists the poll under 9/22/2026. That date matches when the claim first appeared on X. The claim leaves out the 2.3-point margin of error, so the one-point lead is a statistical tie. That omission doesn't make the stated numbers or the attribution wrong. An earlier TSU poll, in August, had the race at 47% to 45%, so the claim isn't confusing the two.

clusters.text: Greg Abbott has won by double digits every time on the ballot and has never trailed a Democrat in an election year.
clusters.verdict_basis:
The election-results half holds up. Ballotpedia and the Center Square list Abbott's margins in six general elections: 
16 points in 2002, 23 in 2006 and 30 in 2010
, then 
more than 20 in 2014, 13 in 2018 and 11 in 2022
. His narrowest win was 2022 (
54.75% to 43.86%
). I did not check his 1996 and 1998 Texas Supreme Court races. The "never trailed a Democrat in an election year" half is contradicted by 2026 polling. 
Fox 7 Austin reported on Sept. 18 that the race "swings to Hinojosa" in a ReconMR poll
. The Hinojosa campaign's release put that poll at 
49–45 for Hinojosa
, though that topline comes from the campaign and I did not confirm it independently. RealClearPolling's table later lists 
several polls with Hinojosa ahead, including NY Times/Siena at 49–46 and YouGov and the University of Texas at 48–47 or 49–48
. Those are mostly after the claim was posted, but the Sept. 17 poll came before it. The claim is therefore half accurate and half contradicted, and the polling half is the part that matters most for its point.
